units.translation: having set before myself mortals in pity, I myself was unable to obtain this

In expressions of this kind the simple τίθεσθαι [to place] is used: the compound is used by Aeschylus, προ πρότερον θέμενος [placing before], before the wretched, as it seems. Nauck (Bulletin de l'Académie de St. Pétersbourg, 1860, p. 240) thought it should be written θνητοὺς δ᾽ ἐν οἴκτῳ θέμενος εἶτ᾽ οἴκτου τυχεῖν οὐκ ἠδυνήθην αὐτός [having placed mortals in pity, then I myself was unable to obtain pity]

Thus Aeschylus in M προσηλούμενον, with υ over α in the first hand, i.e. προσελούμενον, between which two readings the copies fluctuate. The correct reading προυσελοῦμεν is in Arist. Ran. 730 in the Ravenna manuscript, in the Venetian and others προσελοῦμεν, in Stobaeus Flor. 43, 28 προυγελοῦμεν, as in Hesychius προυγελεῖν: προπηλακίζειν, ὑβρίζειν [to insult, to outrage]. The meaning of the verb is clear, but its origin is uncertain, about which there are various opinions of both ancient and recent grammarians, on which see Thes. vol. 6 p. 2084, Hermann in his note on the verse of Aeschylus, Clemm in Ritschl's Acta Soc. philol. vol. 1 p. 77.
